flashcards.q: What's wrong with volumeBindingMode: Immediate for zonal block storage, and what's the default value of this field?
flashcards.a: Immediate IS the default. It binds/provisions the volume before the pod is scheduled, so the provisioner can pick a zone the scheduler later can't place the pod into, causing a permanently unschedulable pod. Use WaitForFirstConsumer for zonal storage.

flashcards.q: reclaimPolicy Delete vs Retain — default, and when to choose Retain?
flashcards.a: Delete is the default for dynamic provisioning — deleting the PVC deletes the underlying volume. Choose Retain for genuinely irreplaceable data (e.g. a database) where accidental PVC deletion silently destroying data is worse than the manual cleanup overhead Retain requires.

flashcards.q: Are Kubernetes Secrets encrypted at rest by default?
flashcards.a: No — base64-encoded only, trivially reversible, fully readable by anyone with etcd access. Real encryption requires explicitly configuring EncryptionConfiguration on the API server with a provider (ideally KMS-backed).

flashcards.q: If you enable EncryptionConfiguration with a KMS provider today, are existing Secrets now protected?
flashcards.a: No — only newly written or updated objects get encrypted under the new config. Existing Secrets remain in their old form until explicitly rewritten (a bulk get/replace pass is the standard follow-up step).

flashcards.q: Local AES key provider vs KMS provider for Secret encryption at rest — what's the real difference?
flashcards.a: Local AES key sits in a file on the control plane, so it doesn't protect against full control-plane compromise. KMS provider never persists key material locally — every encrypt/decrypt calls out to external hardware-backed KMS, giving real separation between etcd access and decrypt capability, plus rotation and audit logging.

flashcards.q: ConfigMap change: volume mount vs env var — which one updates live in a running pod?
flashcards.a: Volume mount syncs live via kubelet's periodic sync (~1 min delay), no restart needed. Env var value is captured once at pod start and never updates without recreating the pod.

flashcards.q: What changed about ServiceAccount tokens in Kubernetes 1.24, and why?
flashcards.a: Stopped auto-generating long-lived, indefinitely-valid Secret-based tokens by default. Instead pods get bound tokens via the TokenRequest API: time-limited (1h default, kubelet-refreshed), audience-bound (API server only), and object-bound (invalid the moment the pod is deleted) — closing the 'leaked token still works months later' incident class.

flashcards.q: How are bound ServiceAccount tokens delivered to pods (1.24+ default)?
flashcards.a: Via a projected volume the kubelet actively refreshes in place, not a static mounted Secret file.

flashcards.q: Role vs ClusterRole, RoleBinding vs ClusterRoleBinding — key distinction and a common reuse pattern?
flashcards.a: Role is always namespace-scoped. ClusterRole is cluster-scoped but can ALSO be bound within just one namespace via an ordinary RoleBinding — a common pattern for defining a reusable permission set once and granting it per-namespace without duplicating the Role object.

flashcards.q: What's the single most commonly flagged RBAC finding in Kubernetes security audits?
flashcards.a: Wildcard grants (resources: ["*"], verbs: ["*"]), typically introduced early to unblock setup and never tightened, effectively granting cluster-admin-equivalent access.

flashcards.q: Why does create access to the serviceaccounts/token subresource need the same scrutiny as the target ServiceAccount's full permissions?
flashcards.a: Anyone with create permission on serviceaccounts/token can mint a fresh bound token impersonating that ServiceAccount at will — functionally equivalent to being granted everything that ServiceAccount can do.

flashcards.q: Why did Kubernetes move storage drivers from in-tree to CSI?
flashcards.a: In-tree plugins were compiled into kubelet/controller-manager, coupling every storage vendor's release cadence to core Kubernetes releases. CSI externalized drivers into independently versioned, out-of-tree plugins decoupled from core release cycles.
